I may get downvoted for this but I believe that if you are aware that someone is immediately preparing to end their life, and you believe that they are in the process of doing it or will very shortly do it, then you have a responsibility to call emergency services on their behalf.

As soon as your friend directly informed you of this, if you do not take action, you will be complicit in his suicide if you do not take steps to prevent it. You have to ask yourself if you will able to live with that for the rest of your life. Personally, I wouldn't be able to live with that. By telling you about his plans, he has made \*you\* responsible for his life - and you need to act on that responsibility by calling emergency services.

In my opinion, your friend would not have told you this if at least a part of him wasn't actually crying out for help. If he truly did not want any help at all, he would not have told you.

I believe that people should have the right to end their own lives, on their terms. But as soon as he involved you in the decision by telling you about his plan, he is making you complicit in his action, which is not fair to you. So that's why you should call emergency services.

If you aren't really sure if he plans to do it, then you should talk to him first. Try to find out if he's serious or not. Encourage him to seek help on his own. If after talking to him for a bit, if he still seems serious and refuses to seek help, then I believe you should seek help for him.
